title: Get oriented in a new repository
prompt: give me an overview of this codebase: architecture, key directories, and how the pieces connect

title: Explain unfamiliar code
prompt:
explain what ${path} does and how data flows through it. write it up as ${format}

Example: path=src/scheduler/queue.ts; format=an HTML page with a diagram, then open it in my browser

title: Find where something happens
prompt:
where do we ${behavior}?

Example: behavior=validate uploaded file types

title: Check what breaks before you delete
prompt:
what would break if I deleted ${target}?

Example: target=the retryWithBackoff helper

title: Trace how code evolved
prompt:
look through the commit history of ${path} and summarize how it evolved and why

Example: path=internal/auth/session.go

title: Scope a change before you start
prompt:
which files would I need to touch to ${change}?

Example: change=add a dark mode toggle to settings

title: Ask the codebase a product question
prompt:
I am a ${role}. walk me through what happens when a user ${action}, from the UI down to the result

Example: role=PM; action=clicks Export to PDF

title: Plan a multi-file change before touching code
prompt:
plan how to refactor the ${target} to ${goal}. list the files you would change, but don't edit anything yet

Example: target=payment module; goal=support multiple currencies

title: Draft a spec by interview
prompt:
I want to build ${feature}. interview me about implementation, UX, edge cases, and tradeoffs until we have covered everything, then write the spec to SPEC.md

Example: feature=per-workspace rate limits

title: Turn a meeting into tickets
prompt:
read ${input} and write up the action items, then create a ticket in ${tracker} for each one, with acceptance criteria

Example: input=@meeting-notes.md; tracker=our issue tracker

title: Map edge cases before building
prompt:
list the error states, empty states, and edge cases for ${feature} that the design needs to cover

Example: feature=the file upload flow

title: Turn a mockup into a working prototype
prompt: here is a mockup. build a working prototype I can click through, matching the layout and states shown

title: Implement from a screenshot and self-check
prompt: implement this design, then take a screenshot of the result, compare it to the original, and fix any differences

title: Follow an existing pattern
prompt:
look at how ${example} is implemented to understand the pattern, then build ${new} the same way

Example: example=the existing webhook handler; new=a payments webhook handler

title: Generate docs for undocumented code
prompt:
find ${scope} without ${format} comments and add them, matching the style already used in the file

Example: scope=the public functions in src/auth/; format=JSDoc

title: Add a small, well-defined feature
prompt:
add a ${endpoint} endpoint that returns ${payload}

Example: endpoint=/health; payload=the app version and uptime

title: Build a small internal tool from scratch
prompt:
create a ${tool} using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, then open it in my browser

Example: tool=drag-and-drop Kanban board with three columns

title: Work an issue end to end
prompt:
read issue #${issue}, implement the fix, and run the tests

Example: issue=312

title: Find and update copy across the codebase
prompt:
find every place we say "${copy}" or a close variant, show me each one in context, then update them all to "${new}". leave tests and the changelog alone

Example: copy=Sign up free; new=Start free trial

title: Draft a document from past examples
prompt:
read the ${examples} in ${folder} to learn the structure and voice, then draft a new one for ${topic}

Example: examples=privacy impact assessments; folder=legal/pia/; topic=the new analytics integration

title: Write tests, run them, fix failures
prompt:
write tests for ${path}, run them, and fix any failures

Example: path=app/parsers/feed.py

title: Drive implementation from tests
prompt:
write tests for ${feature} first, then implement it until they pass

Example: feature=the password reset flow

title: Fill gaps from a coverage report
prompt:
read ${report} and add tests for the lowest-covered files until each is above ${target}%

Example: report=coverage/coverage-summary.json; target=80

title: Migrate a pattern across the codebase
prompt:
migrate everything from ${from} to ${to}: identify every place that needs to change, then make the changes

Example: from=the old logging API; to=the structured logger

title: Port code to another language
prompt:
port ${source} to ${target}, keeping the same ${keep}

Example: source=this Python module; target=Rust; keep=public API and test behavior

title: Optimize against a measurable target
prompt:
optimize ${target} to bring ${metric} from ${current} down to under ${goal}

Example: target=the search query; metric=p95 latency; current=2s; goal=500ms

title: Fix a precise visual bug
prompt:
the ${element} extends ${amount} beyond the ${container} on ${viewport}. fix it.

Example: element=login button; amount=20px; container=card border; viewport=mobile

title: Review your changes before you commit
prompt: review my uncommitted changes and flag anything that looks risky before I commit

title: Review a pull request
prompt:
review PR #${pr} and summarize what changed, then list any concerns

Example: pr=247

title: Review infrastructure changes before applying
prompt: here is my Terraform plan output. what is this going to do, and is anything here going to cause problems?

title: Run a security review with a subagent
prompt:
use a subagent to review ${path} for security issues and report what it finds

Example: path=src/api/

title: Catch issues before formal review
prompt:
review ${file} for ${concerns} and list anything I should fix before it goes to ${reviewer}

Example: file=launch-post.md; concerns=unsupported claims, missing attributions, and brand-guideline issues; reviewer=legal

title: Course-correct a wrong approach
prompt:
that is not right: ${feedback}. try a different approach

Example: feedback=the function signature needs to stay backward-compatible

title: Narrow the scope of a change
prompt:
that is too much. keep only the changes to ${scope} and undo your other edits

Example: scope=the validation logic in src/forms/

title: Turn a correction into a rule
prompt:
you keep ${mistake}. add a rule to CLAUDE.md so this stops happening

Example: mistake=using default exports when this project uses named exports

title: Resolve merge conflicts
prompt: resolve the merge conflicts in this branch and explain what you kept from each side

title: Commit with a generated message
prompt: commit these changes with a message that summarizes what I did

title: Open a pull request from a ticket
prompt:
find the ticket about ${topic} in ${tracker} and open a PR that implements it

Example: tracker=our issue tracker; topic=the login timeout

title: Draft release notes from git history
prompt:
compare ${from} to ${to} and draft release notes grouped by feature, fix, and breaking change

Example: from=v2.3.0; to=v2.4.0

title: Write a CI workflow
prompt:
write a GitHub Actions workflow that ${steps} on every push to ${branch}

Example: steps=runs the tests and deploys to staging; branch=main

title: Find and fix a failing test
prompt:
the ${test} test is failing, find out why and fix it

Example: test=UserAuth

title: Investigate a reported error
prompt:
users are seeing ${symptom} on ${where}. investigate and tell me what is going on

Example: symptom=500 errors; where=/api/settings

title: Fix a build error at the root
prompt: here is a build error. fix the root cause and verify the build succeeds

title: Investigate a production incident
prompt:
${symptom}. check the logs, recent deploys, and config changes, then tell me the most likely cause

Example: symptom=the checkout endpoint started returning 500s an hour ago

title: Diagnose from a console screenshot
prompt:
here is a screenshot of ${console}. walk me through why ${resource} is failing and give me the exact commands to fix it

Example: console=our Kubernetes dashboard; resource=this pod

title: Query logs in plain English
prompt:
show me all ${events} for ${scope} over ${timeframe}. write the query, run it, and tell me what stands out

Example: events=failed logins; scope=the auth service; timeframe=the past 24 hours

title: Analyze a data file
prompt:
read ${file}, summarize the key patterns, and write the results to ${output}

Example: file=@reports/q1-signups.csv; output=an HTML page with charts, then open it in my browser

title: Generate variations from performance data
prompt:
read ${file}, find the underperforming ${items}, and generate ${n} new variations that stay under ${limit} characters

Example: file=@ads-performance.csv; items=headlines; n=20; limit=90

title: Turn a recurring task into a skill
prompt:
create a /${name} skill for this project that ${steps}

Example: name=ship; steps=runs the linter and tests, then drafts a commit message

title: Add a hook for repeat behavior
prompt:
write a hook that ${action} after every ${event}

Example: action=runs prettier; event=edit to a .ts or .tsx file

title: Connect a tool with MCP
prompt:
connect ${server} via MCP so you can read its ${data} directly

Example: server=our error tracker; data=stack traces

title: Capture what to remember for next time
prompt: summarize what we did this session and suggest what to add to CLAUDE.md
